title: Blood vessels
summary: The network of arteries, veins and capillaries that carries blood everywhere.

layers.basics: Blood vessels are the body's plumbing: arteries carry blood out, capillaries exchange materials, and veins bring blood back.
layers.deeper: Arteries have thick muscular walls, veins have valves and thin walls, and capillaries are one cell thick.
layers.expert: Total resistance is set mainly by arterioles; vessel tone is regulated by endothelial NO, sympathetic nerves, and angiotensin II; angiogenesis is driven by VEGF.

did_you_know: If all your capillaries were laid end to end they would circle Earth more than once by the usual estimate, though that figure is approximate.

title: Synapse
summary: The tiny junction where one neuron signals to the next.

layers.basics: A synapse is a microscopic gap across which chemical messengers pass.
layers.deeper: The gap (cleft) is about 20 nanometers wide; vesicles on one side release neurotransmitter onto receptors on the other.
layers.expert: Active zone with Ca2+ channels and docked vesicles; postsynaptic density with scaffold PSD-95; AMPA/NMDA receptor trafficking underlies LTP; ≈ 10^14-10^15 synapses in the human brain.

did_you_know: The brain's synapse count is in the hundreds of trillions.

title: Neuromuscular junction
summary: The synapse where a motor neuron commands a muscle fiber.

layers.basics: This is where nerve meets muscle, using the chemical acetylcholine.
layers.deeper: One motor neuron's terminal releases acetylcholine onto receptors on the muscle fiber.
layers.expert: Nicotinic ACh receptors (≈ 10^4 µm⁻²) produce end-plate potentials, with a high safety factor; acetylcholinesterase ends the signal; targeted by curare and botulinum toxin.

did_you_know: Botulinum toxin paralyzes muscle by blocking acetylcholine release here.

title: Tendon
summary: A tough cord of collagen joining muscle to bone.

layers.basics: Tendons transmit the pull of muscles to bones.
layers.deeper: They are strong but poorly supplied with blood, so heal slowly.
layers.expert: Parallel type I collagen with tenocytes; stores elastic energy (Achilles ≈ 35% of running work); tensile strength ≈ 50-100 MPa.

did_you_know: The Achilles tendon can handle loads of several times body weight.
